Class StorageAttachments

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.core.attachment.StorageAttachments
public final class StorageAttachments extends Object
Fabric attachment-type registry for M7. Each consumer-declared StorageAttachment registers exactly one attachment per owner type with a unique identifier — the library maintains this registry so registrations are idempotent and inspectable.

Attachments store ItemContainerContents (vanilla's codec-backed item-list type) and the Storage surface converts to/from mutable NonNullList on each read/write. Using ItemContainerContents lets M7 reuse vanilla's codec directly instead of composing a NonNullList codec.

Not public API — consumers go through StorageAttachment's factories, which call into this registry internally.

  • Method Details

    • registerContainerAttachment

      public static net.fabricmc.fabric.api.attachment.v1.AttachmentType<net.minecraft.world.item.component.ItemContainerContents> registerContainerAttachment(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier id, int defaultSlots)
      Register (or retrieve) an attachment storing ItemContainerContents. Persistence is automatic via Fabric's .persistent(Codec).

      Use this variant for non-block-scoped attachments (player-attached, item-attached, ephemeral, custom). For block-scoped attachments, use registerBlockScopedAttachment(Identifier, int) instead — same underlying registration, plus the block-scoped registry entry for drop-on-break dispatch.

      Parameters:
      id - the attachment's unique identifier (shows up in NBT paths)
      defaultSlots - number of slots in the default empty content

    • registerPlayerContentAttachment

      public static net.fabricmc.fabric.api.attachment.v1.AttachmentType<net.minecraft.world.item.component.ItemContainerContents> registerPlayerContentAttachment(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier id, int defaultSlots)
      Register (or retrieve) a PLAYER content attachment — like registerContainerAttachment(Identifier, int) but with Fabric's copyOnDeath() flag (so a KEPT bag carries across respawn) plus enrollment in the player death-drop registry at DropRule.DEFAULT (zero-config vanilla parity). The death handler (PlayerDeathDropHandler) iterates the registry and owns the keepInventory check; the consumer overrides the per-attachment rule via StorageAttachment.dropsOnDeath(...). Called by StorageAttachment.playerAttached(String, String, int).

      Register a block-scoped attachment. Same as registerContainerAttachment(Identifier, int) plus enrollment in the block-scoped registry that the drop-on-break mixin dispatches against. Called by StorageAttachment.blockScoped(String, String, int).

    • registerCustomPlayerDeathSpec

      public static void registerCustomPlayerDeathSpec(CustomAttachmentSpec<?,?> spec, DropRule rule)
      Enroll a player-anchored custom spec for death handling at rule (or override the rule for an already-enrolled spec). Called by StorageAttachment.customPlayerAttached(spec).dropsOnDeath(rule). The owner type is statically Player (the typed factory enforces it), so a non-player spec can never reach this. The library owns the gamerule-gated DROP/DESTROY; the consumer's storage owns KEEP-across-respawn survival.
